newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes flat in quiet market, wet cargoes immobile.
newsitem.headline: Crudes flat in quiet market, wet cargoes immobile.

text.p: Crude oil prices were mostly unchanged in a quiet market lacking fresh factors to provide direction, and participants mostly retreated to the sidelines, traders said on Monday.
The NYMEX energy market will be closed on Monday for the U.S. President"s Day holiday and traders said this was an additional factor discouraging activity.
"It"s difficult to make a move when the market"s almost dead," one Japanese trader said.
Cash April Brent was notionally assessed at $20.45/20.55, the same as late-U.S. trading levels on Friday.
SIMEX Brent crude futures were untraded at 0340 GMT, with indications far apart. The April Brent contract was bid at $20.30 and offered at $20.75.
No indications for spread were available.
Physical trading in Gulf crudes was also quiet with many Japanese market participants still pondering their positions for April cargoes.
Most traders agreed that premiums for April cargoes were likely to start weaker than those for March.
Some market participants said trading could begin with medium crude grades including Oman, as seasonal demand for lighter crudes was about over.
